feed.title: Mobile & Desktop — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Android Developers
entry.summary: The official Android developer documentation, tools and guides.

entry.title: Apple Developer
entry.summary: The official developer documentation and resources for iOS and Apple platforms.

entry.title: Awesome Android
entry.summary: A list of libraries, tools and learning resources for Android development. Unlike general search it is split into categories from architecture to UI.

entry.title: Awesome Capacitor
entry.summary: A resource list for Capacitor, wrapping web apps in a native mobile shell.

entry.title: Awesome Cordova
entry.summary: A resource list for Cordova, building hybrid mobile apps with JavaScript.

entry.title: Awesome Electron
entry.summary: A resource list for Electron, building desktop apps with web technologies.

entry.title: Awesome Flutter
entry.summary: A list of packages, samples and tutorials for building cross-platform apps with Flutter. Unlike the official catalog it brings together community packages and real app examples.

entry.title: Awesome iOS
entry.summary: A list of libraries, tools and learning resources for iOS development. Unlike general Apple lists it focuses on the iOS app layer and the Swift/Obj-C ecosystem.

entry.title: Awesome React Native
entry.summary: A list of components and tools for mobile development with React Native. Unlike web React lists it focuses on native mobile components and bridges.

entry.title: Awesome Scriptable
entry.summary: A resource list for Scriptable, the iOS app for automation in JavaScript.

entry.title: Awesome Smart TV
entry.summary: A resource list for building apps across different TV platforms.

entry.title: Awesome Swift
entry.summary: A list of libraries and tools for Apple’s Swift language. Unlike general iOS lists it focuses directly on the language and its packages.

entry.title: Awesome Uno Platform
entry.summary: A list for Uno Platform, building cross-platform .NET UIs from one codebase.

entry.title: Awesome watchOS
entry.summary: A resource list for Apple Watch (watchOS) app development.

entry.title: Capacitor
entry.summary: A native runtime that wraps a web app in a native shell with access to device APIs.

entry.title: CocoaPods
entry.summary: A widely used dependency manager for iOS and Apple projects.

entry.title: fastlane
entry.summary: An open-source tool that automates mobile builds, screenshots and store releases.

entry.title: Hacking with Swift
entry.summary: Learn Swift and SwiftUI through projects, known for its free "100 Days" courses.

entry.title: Ionic
entry.summary: An open-source framework for building cross-platform mobile UIs with web technologies.

entry.title: Kodeco
entry.summary: In-depth mobile-development tutorials for iOS, Android and Flutter (formerly raywenderlich).

entry.title: Material Design
entry.summary: Google's open design system and UI guidelines — the basis of the Android interface.

entry.title: NativeScript
entry.summary: Builds truly native mobile apps from JavaScript, TypeScript, Vue or Angular.

entry.title: objc.io
entry.summary: Books and video series on advanced Swift and iOS.

entry.title: ProAndroidDev
entry.summary: A community publication of advanced Android-engineering articles.

entry.title: pub.dev
entry.summary: The official package registry for Dart and Flutter.

entry.title: React Native
entry.summary: The official docs of the cross-platform framework for building native mobile apps with React.

entry.title: Swift by Sundell
entry.summary: Deep articles and a podcast on Swift, by John Sundell.

entry.title: XDA Forums
entry.summary: The largest community forum for Android device modding, ROMs and root. Unlike general forums it is split device by device into deep technical threads.

entry.title: Awesome Android Root
entry.summary: A knowledge base for rooting Android with 600+ apps, Magisk/KernelSU/APatch/LSPosed modules and device-specific guides. Unlike scattered forum threads it is organised: it gathers step-by-step guides for devices like Pixel, Samsung and Xiaomi in one place.

entry.title: OpenAPK
entry.summary: A daily-updated, categorised list of open-source apps and games for Android. Unlike repositories such as F-Droid it is a directory, not a store: it points apps straight to their own source repositories, with no package distribution of its own.

entry.title: Android Weekly
entry.summary: A weekly newsletter of Android and Kotlin development news: articles, libraries, jobs. Against following blogs it is curated — one email a week instead of chasing scattered feeds.

entry.title: Don't Kill My App
entry.summary: Documents how each Android manufacturer kills background apps, brand by brand, with the workaround for each device. Unlike general Android documentation it is per-vendor — which is where the answer to "why did my alarm not ring" lives.

entry.title: Exodus Privacy
entry.summary: Reports the trackers and permissions inside Android apps. Unlike Play Store privacy labels it reads the APK rather than the declaration — what the developer shipped, not what they said.

entry.title: Fossdroid
entry.summary: A browsable showcase of the free-software Android apps in the F-Droid repository. Against the F-Droid client it offers discovery by popularity on the web — you can see which apps are actually used.

entry.title: Godot
entry.summary: An MIT-licensed game engine with separately mature 2D and 3D pipelines. Where it parts ways with Unity and Unreal is the licence: no revenue share, no seat fee, no per-install charge — the whole engine is yours.

entry.title: IzzyOnDroid
entry.summary: An additional F-Droid repository carrying apps that are open source but not in the official repo, each run through a privacy audit. Against the official repository it updates faster and publishes a tracker report.

entry.title: microStudio
entry.summary: A complete game development environment in the browser: code editor, sprite drawing, map editor and sound generation together. Unlike Godot or Unity it installs nothing, so it works on a Chromebook — which makes it good for teaching.

entry.title: Open 3D Engine
entry.summary: Amazon’s Lumberyard, handed to the Linux Foundation as an Apache 2.0 modular 3D engine. Heavier than Godot, but with a rendering pipeline closer to AAA scale — the open-source option for teams that want corporate backing.

entry.title: Unreal Engine
entry.summary: The engine behind AAA productions, offering real-time high-density geometry and global illumination through Nanite and Lumen. Against Unity it wins on visual ceiling and Blueprint visual scripting, and pays for it with heavier projects and a steeper climb.

entry.title: ThinMatrix
entry.summary: An indie developer’s devlog alongside an OpenGL tutorial series. Unlike engine tutorials he writes the engine from scratch, which shows what sits underneath the abstraction.
